title: Plant foot, striking surface and lean

items.stem: A kicker plants the non-kicking foot well behind the ball and strikes through the centre of the ball. Which effect on the kicking foot at contact explains why the shot tends to rise?

options.text: The foot is already past the bottom of its swing and moving upward
The foot is moving level but strikes the ball with less speed
The foot is at the bottom of its swing and moving downward
The foot is moving level but strikes the ball with more spin

items.stem: A penalty is taken from 11 m. The kick leaves with an angle error of 2 degrees to the side of the aim line. Using lateral miss = 11 x tan(error), how far, in metres, does the ball finish from the aim point? Give two decimal places.
A kicker wants to place the ball 0.4 m inside the post and has a wide error spread with the laces. Which choice best matches the trade-off between power and accuracy?

options.text: Use the laces and swing harder to beat the keeper's reaction
Use the laces but plant further back for a longer swing
Use the inside of the foot for a tighter spread with some power loss
Use the inside of the foot and lean back to add more power

items.stem: A kicker corrects only a backward lean by standing more upright, yet shots still go over the bar. In one sentence, which other input should the kicker correct, according to the lesson's sources?
Where on the ball should the foot make contact to keep a penalty low and still get good speed?

options.text: Slightly below the centre, to add lift and clear the keeper
Slightly above the centre, to press the ball into the ground
On the very bottom edge, to maximise the foot's follow-through
At the centre of the ball, so the contact stays level
